info.description:
Development API of LeafWiki. This documentation is incomplete, experimental and may change before v1; only a few operations are described so far.
API keys (Bearer authentication) are available only when LeafWiki runs with `--enable-api-key-management` and authentication enabled. Existing browser API routes are not newly hidden behind that flag.
Browser sessions use the access and refresh cookies (`__Host-leafwiki_at` and `__Host-leafwiki_rt` on secure connections, unprefixed names for allowed insecure development). Session writes are protected by CSRF double-submit: send the `X-CSRF-Token` header matching the CSRF cookie (the `csrf_token` form field is accepted as a fallback).
The documented base path is the default mount. A deployment started with `--base-path=/wiki` prepends `/wiki` to every documented URL.
info.title: LeafWiki API

get.description: Public liveness and readiness probe; no authentication is required and session cookies are never validated. Global middleware can still reject a request before the handler runs: 401 for an invalid, revoked or expired API key (only when API-key management is enabled) or for an identity asserted by a trusted reverse proxy that LeafWiki rejects (only when reverse-proxy authentication is enabled), and 429 when API-key attempts are throttled.

200.description: All checks passed (ongoing search indexing still counts as healthy)

401.description: Invalid, revoked or expired API key (when API-key management is enabled), or a rejected trusted-proxy identity: unknown user or auto-provisioning email conflict (when reverse-proxy authentication is enabled)

503.description: Degraded: the body is a HealthResponse with failed checks. If API-key resolution cannot reach its store, the body is a LegacyError instead. Swagger 2.0 cannot express this alternative, so the schema is a broad object.

get.description:
Lists the frontmatter property keys with the number of pages carrying each, ordered by count (descending), then by key. Nested properties use dot-joined keys such as `a.b`.
Access: a signed-in user (session cookie, API key or reverse-proxy identity); anonymous callers only when public access is on. With public access on, a missing or invalid session cookie is treated as anonymous instead of 401.

parameters.description: Prefix filter on the key; trimmed and lowercased before matching
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: Maximum number of keys; values below 1 mean 50, values above 200 mean 200
parameters.name: limit

200.description: Keys with page counts; empty array when nothing matches

400.description: limit is not an integer (code properties_invalid_limit)

401.description: No valid session while public access is off, an invalid, revoked or expired API key (when API-key management is enabled), or a rejected trusted-proxy identity (when reverse-proxy authentication is enabled)

500.description: Index lookup failed: the body is an ErrorResponse (code properties_internal_error). Authentication middleware failures return a LegacyError instead. Swagger 2.0 cannot express this alternative, so the schema is a broad object.

503.description: API-key store unavailable during a live restore (when API-key management is enabled)

get.description:
Lists the pages whose property `key` has exactly the value `value`. Key and value are matched as given (not trimmed or lowercased); each must contain a non-space character.
Access: a signed-in user (session cookie, API key or reverse-proxy identity); anonymous callers only when public access is on. With public access on, a missing or invalid session cookie is treated as anonymous instead of 401.

parameters.description: Property key, for example `status` or a dot-joined nested key
parameters.name: key

200.description: Matching pages with all their properties; empty array when none match

400.description: key or value is missing or blank (code properties_missing_key or properties_missing_value)

401.description: No valid session while public access is off, an invalid, revoked or expired API key (when API-key management is enabled), or a rejected trusted-proxy identity (when reverse-proxy authentication is enabled)

500.description: Index lookup failed: the body is an ErrorResponse (code properties_internal_error). Authentication middleware failures return a LegacyError instead. Swagger 2.0 cannot express this alternative, so the schema is a broad object.

503.description: API-key store unavailable during a live restore (when API-key management is enabled)

get.description:
Lists tags with the number of pages carrying each, ordered by count (descending), then by tag. With `selected`, only pages carrying every selected tag are counted and the selected tags themselves are left out, so the result is the tags that can narrow the selection further.
Access: a signed-in user (session cookie, API key or reverse-proxy identity); anonymous callers only when public access is on. With public access on, a missing or invalid session cookie is treated as anonymous instead of 401.

parameters.description: Prefix filter on the tag name; trimmed and lowercased before matching
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: Maximum number of tags; values below 1 mean 50, values above 200 mean 200
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: Already selected tags; repeat the parameter or separate tags with commas
parameters.name: selected

200.description: Tags with page counts; empty array when nothing matches

400.description: limit is not an integer (code tags_invalid_limit)

401.description: No valid session while public access is off, an invalid, revoked or expired API key (when API-key management is enabled), or a rejected trusted-proxy identity (when reverse-proxy authentication is enabled)

500.description: Index lookup failed: the body is an ErrorResponse (code tags_internal_error). Authentication middleware failures return a LegacyError instead. Swagger 2.0 cannot express this alternative, so the schema is a broad object.

503.description: API-key store unavailable during a live restore (when API-key management is enabled)

get.description:
Lists the pages that carry every given tag. Tags are trimmed and lowercased before matching.
Access: a signed-in user (session cookie, API key or reverse-proxy identity); anonymous callers only when public access is on. With public access on, a missing or invalid session cookie is treated as anonymous instead of 401.

parameters.description: Tags a page must all carry; repeat the parameter or separate tags with commas
parameters.name: tags

200.description: Matching pages; empty array when none match

401.description: No valid session while public access is off, an invalid, revoked or expired API key (when API-key management is enabled), or a rejected trusted-proxy identity (when reverse-proxy authentication is enabled)

500.description: Index lookup failed: the body is an ErrorResponse (code tags_internal_error). Authentication middleware failures return a LegacyError instead. Swagger 2.0 cannot express this alternative, so the schema is a broad object.

args.description: Args are the values substituted into Template; omitted when empty.

code.description: Code is the stable machine-readable error code, e.g. "page_not_found".

message.description: Message is the English human-readable message.

template.description:
Template is the localization key the client translates; it doubles as
the fallback message when no translation exists.

error.description: Error carries the localizable error details.
Error is the human-readable error message.

checks.description:
Checks maps each check name (sqlite, data_dir, search) to its result:
"ok" or "failed" for sqlite and data_dir; "ok", "indexing" or "failed" for search.

status.description: Status is "ok" when every check passes, otherwise "degraded".

BearerAuth.description: API key sent as the entire header value `Bearer lw_<prefix>_<secret>`, not just the secret. A request authenticated by a resolved key acts with the effective role of the lesser of the key owner's role and the key's role. A resolved key skips CSRF checks; a header merely being present does not. Routes that reject API-key authentication are browser-session only and say so. Cookies remain an alternative authentication path and are described in prose because Swagger 2.0 cannot express them.
